governance.note: neiso-55 = the neiso-54 keeper recipe (byte-identical run_config, CLI flags, the three winter fuel-security mechanisms and the CT evening-ramp / ST_GAS->Component-B reliability drag in reliability_floor_coeffs_NEISO.csv) with ONE structural addition: temp_dependent_derate=True. This replaces the flat EIA-860 net-summer / _SUMMER_CLASS_DERATE thermal-capacity treatment with a per-class dry-bulb-temperature derate curve (fleet.generators_to_fleet_arrays): CC/CT get a capacity-NEUTRAL reshape rescaled so the Jun-Sep mean reproduces the existing net-summer capability (heatwave hours fall below net-summer, cooler hours rise toward full rating); COAL/ST_GAS gain a pure additive hot-hour derate; nuclear is excluded; zones without weather coverage fall back to the flat derate; availability is clipped to [0,1]. The mechanism is physically grounded (gas-turbine air-density/mass-flow limits, steam condenser limits; arXiv:2311.07001, CPUC R.21-10-002) and its slopes/reference temps are physical constants in ScenarioConfig, NOT tuned to the backcast. It is promoted on rule-1 STRUCTURAL fidelity, NOT on a backcast improvement. Fit effect on NEISO is neutral-to-mixed and is recorded honestly: C3a mean-LMP improved to all-PASS (2023 -3.7%, 2024 -1.8%, 2025 +4.3%; was CAVEAT/-5.5% in 2023 on neiso-54); C3c scarcity tail UNCHANGED at 0h vs the ledgered winter scarcity-price-formation gap (temp_dependent_derate is dormant on it - the summer/shoulder reshape does not tighten winter cold-hour capacity, so the >$300 tail still does not form, model 0h max ~$258, unchanged vs the zero-forcing ablation twin); C5b storage throughput is marginally deeper (-60.2% vs -56.3% on neiso-54), the same downstream-of-winter-scarcity item. No lever is fitted to a price residual and no input is pinned to actuals.

exceptions.metric: hours LMP > $300/MWh (C3c scarcity tail, DA-expressible / NEISO $300 threshold)
exceptions.magnitude: model 0h vs DA actual 5h (RT 15h); system max ~$258
exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (NEISO winter scarcity-price formation; winter fuel-security build adopted, DORMANT on this backcast; temp_dependent_derate also dormant on the tail)
exceptions.reason: The energy-only LP caps the cold-hour price at dual-fuel oil-parity (~$258/MWh). The adopted winter fuel-inventory / seasonal-reliability build (neiso_gas_coldsnap_derate + neiso_winter_fuel_inventory + neiso_winter_fuel_mustrun) is DORMANT on 2023-2025: the derate removes too little capacity on too few hours to make the ample NEISO winter fleet reserve-short, so Component A's oil budget never binds and the >$300 tail does not form (model 0h, unchanged vs the zero-forcing ablation twin). temp_dependent_derate does NOT change this: its CC/CT reshape is capacity-neutral over summer and its additive COAL/ST_GAS hot-hour derate does not touch the winter cold-hour hours where NEISO's tail actually forms - hoursGt300 is 0h in every year with and without the derate. This is a winter capacity-adequacy / scarcity-price-formation gap, NOT closable by these mechanisms here and NEVER by an offer adder tuned to the tail.

exceptions.magnitude: model 0.83 vs actual 2.08 TWh (-60.2%; was -56.3% / 0.91 TWh on the neiso-54 keeper)
exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (downstream of the price_tail / winter-scarcity item)
exceptions.reason: PS arbitrage throughput tracks the intraday price spread. The residual under-cycle is winter-concentrated: the LP's cold-month spread stays compressed at the dual-fuel oil-parity cap, and the real Northfield fleet additionally cycles near-daily for reserves/regulation the energy-only LP does not remunerate. Per the neiso-ps-undercycling diagnosis the PS number may only move DOWNSTREAM of price structure, never via a storage knob. temp_dependent_derate slightly DEEPENS the gap (-56.3% -> -60.2%): the capacity-neutral summer reshape trims a little of the shoulder-season spread the PS fleet was arbitraging, without adding winter spread. Closes only with the winter fuel-inventory build and/or in-LP reserve co-optimization value reaching storage; never via a storage knob.

exceptions.metric: C2 gas family grid-delivered TWh (preliminary 2025 vintage)
exceptions.magnitude: +2.6% vs corrected EIA-930 grid gas (commercial band)
exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (EIA-930 gas-vs-OTHER fold-in + preliminary-vintage incompleteness)
exceptions.reason: 2025 is a preliminary EIA-923 vintage - per-class actuals are incomplete (13/30 prior CC_REGULAR plants missing, 57% reporting). The scorer falls back to the EIA-930 grid gas cell, which includes geothermal+biomass; the correction formula under-corrects because the preliminary vintage's per-class cells are incomplete. Same categorization issue as the complete-vintage years, where the per-class C1 gate PASSES under the load-scaled band. NOT closable by adjusting model dispatch. Unchanged by temp_dependent_derate.

exceptions.metric: C1 coal + steam-gas winter-energy under-run (within the C1 band, non-gating; documentation)
exceptions.magnitude: COAL_BIT model ~0.06/0.11/0.23 vs actual 0.18/0.24/0.27 TWh (2023/24/25); ST_GAS similar
exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (structural; same winter fuel-security family as price_tail and storage)
exceptions.reason: The energy-only LP runs coal/steam only at the temperature-floor commitment plus the hours delivered gas is dear enough; the real units ran more on winter fuel-security / local-reliability commitments. Closable only via the documented winter fuel-inventory / seasonal-reliability build, never by cranking the floor slope/cap or an offer adder. Within the C1 band, non-gating. Unchanged by temp_dependent_derate.

neiso-55 adds temp_dependent_derate on the neiso-54 recipe, so a fresh zero-forcing ablation (--zero-forcing-ablation, same recipe + temp_dependent_derate, full 2023-2025 span, all merchant floors/bridges off) is registered as 2026-07-09-neiso-55-temp-derate and linked from this keeper's sidecar ablation_twin field (audit_keepers.py E9).
